newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev falls to new low in illiquid market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev falls to new low in illiquid market.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at an all-time low of 885-890 per dollar versus its opening at 860-880 and 810-815 at Wednesday's close due to dwindling foreign currency supply, dealers said.

"Even demand for small amounts of dollars instantly pressures the lev. Supply was very low due to uncertainty among traders over the outcome of the current political crisis, which has delayed funding talks with the IMF," a dealer said.
Traders said that no big final clients were seen bidding for dollars today but almost all banks have actively sought foreign currency in anticipation of an ongoing sharp lev fall.

The recent rapid lev depreciation is likely to accelerate in coming days because the central bank was not able to intervene significantly and the high central interest rate can no longer deter the fall, another dealer said.
The lev traded near 600 to the dollar at the beginning of January. The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) main interest rate now is 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually.
The BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov has said that the bank will give priority to foreign debt payments and could provide only a limited support to the lev because of its low foreign exchange reserves.

Reserves stood at $518 million at end-December. Bulgaria has pledged to pay $135 million coupon on its Brady bonds next week out of a total of $300 million foreign debt payments due in the first quarter.

Bulgaria urgently needs a credible government to negotiate funding from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which has suspended disbursements because the outgoing Socialist government has not followed previous reform programmes.

The IMF has said it is ready to resume negotiations on the implementation of a strict fixed exchange rate regime, seen as a last resort to save the crumbling economy from collapse, as soon as a new government is in place.

Bulgaria's new president Petar Stoyanov met leaders of warring political factions on Thursday to seek a way out of the deadlock blocking formation of a new government, but there was no immediate sign of a breakthrough.
